A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the traditional Eritreans’ way of life, their cultural values, social organization, and their economic system have been and still are the most important determinants for the way they cope with risks in general and health risks in particular.
traditional risk-sharing arrangements and social insurance schemes are complementary and mutually reinforcing.

The main takeaway from our work is that
in the absence of formal insurance, traditional risk-sharing arrangements can be used to provide social insurance to low-income populations.

in the absence of formal social insurance schemes, the extension of mutual aid community associations into Mahber-based health schemes at the local community level is the only way to provide modern health services to the poor.
the Mahber system can be used as a basis for health insurance schemes that are more affordable and sustainable.
